text:
maya: FYI — BrightWave is asking what evidence we need to avoid SLA credits for their embedded UX migration next week. They want 99.95% uptime and p95 latency <300ms during the cutover window. Can CS ops list required artifacts?

jonathan: got it. need account id + exact migration window. also confirm whether they’re using hosted API or Dedicated.

maya: account BW-8821, migration window 2025-05-01T02:00 to 2025-05-03T10:00 UTC. Hosted API (standard tier) with burst to dedicated for traffic spike.

samir: ok — from SRE side we’ll need: 1) per-minute uptime vector for the window, 2) p95 latency time series broken out by route, 3) any scaled failures / 5xx counts, and 4) sample request/response ids for any anomalous minutes.

samir: quick query you can paste into the metrics console:

```
# pseudo-query - metrics dashboard
SELECT
  floor(timestamp, 1m) AS minute,
  count_if(code >= 500) AS errors,
  100 - (count_if(code >= 500) / count(*)) * 100 AS uptime_pct,
  percentile(latency_ms, 95) AS p95_ms
FROM requests
WHERE account_id = 'BW-8821' AND timestamp BETWEEN '2025-05-01T02:00:00Z' AND '2025-05-03T10:00:00Z'
GROUP BY minute
ORDER BY minute;
```

samir: send me the raw CSV output and i’ll produce the minute-by-minute proof and a summarized sliding-window claim (5m and 1h).

ops-bot: deploy-notice: autoscaler will add burst pool 2025-05-01T01:45 UTC -> 2025-05-03T11:00 UTC for BW-8821.

amanda: renewal is on 2025-05-15 — if we can show compliance during migration that helps the renewal motion. also capture any UX feedback that could affect feature commitments.

emily: tagging UX team — can we get a short survey of any frontend errors (JS fetch timeouts) during that window? frontend failures might look like our latency but are client-side. We should separate them in the report.

maya: good call. list of artifacts compiled so far: [1] per-minute uptime CSV, [2] p95/p50 latency time series by route, [3] 5xx counts and root-cause notes, [4] sample request IDs and payloads for anomalous minutes, [5] autoscaler / burst config and timeline, [6] frontend error summary (UX). anything else?

jonathan: also include the alerts timeline (pagerduty incidents) and any manual interventions. timestamps for operator actions are important for dispute windows.

samir: will add a short runbook excerpt: what fallback model was used and when (we had automatic fallback to smaller model variant). include the model variant mapping to cost/latency.

maya: BrightWave asked whether CS can pre-approve the evidence package to avoid a formal credit claim process. can legal/signing approve a light acceptance checklist?

amanda: i can draft an acceptance checklist but legal needs to OK — propose the checklist be: (A) uptime >=99.95% rolling during migration OR (B) documented outage with timeline + remediation and arbitration window. also a clause for partial credits if p95 slipped >300ms for more than 30 continuous minutes.

emily: for internal notes — capture qualitative feedback during migration (dropdown in ticket): slow initial load, intermittent timeouts, token refresh errors. we’ll attach a one-pager "Customer migration UX observations".

maya: action items: samir will run the metrics query and attach raw CSV (due 2025-05-04). emily will gather frontend error summary (due 2025-05-04). amanda will draft the acceptance checklist and send to legal for review (due 2025-04-28). jonathan will capture operator intervention logs and PD incidents (due 2025-05-05).

samir: starting the query now. will post progress and the CSV to the thread when ready.

maya: thanks — please ping me when CSV posted. BrightWave is anxious about avoiding credits but also wants clear guardrails. :eyes:

amanda: noted. i’ll align the renewal owner and include the migration evidence in the renewal pack if all looks good. :thumbsup:

jonathan: once we have artifacts, recommend a 15-min readout with the customer where we walk the evidence and sign the checklist live. reduces escalation.

maya: agreed. scheduling a readout tentatively 2025-05-06 16:00 UTC. i’ll send invite after we have the initial artifacts.

ops-bot: note: alert suppression will be enabled for BW-8821 during the migration window to avoid alert fatigue. see #eng-oncall for suppression policy.

samir: CSV export uploaded: https://redwood-internal/storage/exports/BW-8821-migration-20250501-03.csv — posted to the thread.

maya: received. i’ll review and draft the evidence summary, then circulate to legal + renewal owner. thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
